material_findings.title: DARPA D2 Sprint opens a $1M autonomous medical-documentation and decision-support competition
material_findings.summary: DARPA's Documentation and Decision Support Sprint is a current virtual AI/algorithm competition with $1,000,000 total prizes across Documentation and Decision Support tracks. DARPA lists rolling qualification through Dec. 1, a Nov. 4 Part 1 narrative deadline, Dec. 1 Part 2 deadline, up to 20 qualified teams, and a Mar. 1, 2027 final algorithm-package deadline. Each track pays $300,000 / $150,000 / $50,000 for first through third. Primary terms establish U.S.-representative eligibility, prize/TIN conditions, limited-use DARPA datasets, no re-identification/facial-recognition/profiling, and isolated Docker-based qualification evaluation on simulated-casualty data.
material_findings.recommended_action: When chronological integration reaches this contribution, reopen the current DARPA D2 rules/resources and registration surface, confirm whether participant eligibility and registration intent exist, and only then create a structured competition case. If pursued, keep all DARPA-provided data within the published local-development scope, preserve the exact rule/document versions, and treat medical/algorithm outputs as competition artifacts rather than validated clinical capability.

DARPA D2 data authorization is limited to the competition terms: local development/training for the Sprint, with explicit prohibitions on unauthorized sharing, re-identification, facial recognition, profiling and biometric surveillance. No controlled dataset was downloaded or used in this pass.
